correctness.rationale: A path in a spider uses at most two arms, and leaf endpoints realize the selected counts in any two arms. Therefore max selected on any geodesic is the sum of the largest two arm counts. This proves the exhaustive face trichotomy, facet dichotomy and purity boundary without computational assumptions. When all arms have two edges, the complex is the union of d closed d-balls along the common cross-polytope (d-1)-sphere; relative cellular homology gives the integral sign-twisted augmentation kernel and explicit d-1-sphere wedge. A standalone geodesic BFS checker exhaustively confirms 52 length-tuples and homology/sign actions for d=2..5. Finite tests are supporting, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is the first higher-arity k=4 level beyond the original k=3 edge general position problem, whose tree maximum was already known. The complete face and facet polynomials for all spiders give a sharp purity boundary and an unbounded maximal-face-size gap, while equal two-edge arms exhibit a mixed-threshold phenomenon: their k=4 complex is a wedge of d-1 spheres in dimension d with an exact integral arm-permutation sign-twisted augmentation lattice. This adds natural structural and equivariant invariants beyond a scalar maximum or a routine parameter increment.
